name: China economy
summary: China property investment fell 21.6% in January to October and fixed-asset investment 8.1%; slump persists
state: Property investment fell 21.6% in the first ten months of 2026 and fixed-asset investment 8.1%, while October retail sales rose only 0.4% year on year and home prices kept falling, according to data released on 16 Nov (The Edge Malaysia). Growth of 4.6% in the first three quarters sits at the low end of the 4.5–5% target. The property slump keeps the signal at Watch; no hard landing below 3%, wider financial contagion or sharp tightening of capital controls was found as of 25 Nov.
for_you: Firms selling to Chinese consumers or exposed to Chinese property and construction face weak demand. Commodity exporters may see softer orders from China.
rubric_hit: Watch: property slump (investment −21.6% Jan–Oct) and growth at low end of target; no hard landing <3%

sources.title: The Edge Malaysia — China economic data for October (16 Nov 2026)

why: China is the world's factory and the biggest marginal buyer of commodities; a hard landing would ripple through every supply chain.
drivers: Property sector, local-government debt, exports and tariffs, deflation, stimulus.

rubric.alert: Hard landing (growth < 3%), financial contagion, or capital controls tightened sharply.
rubric.watch: Deflation, renewed property-developer defaults, or growth clearly below target.
rubric.normal: Growth near official target, stable property sales, no financial contagion.
